steps.body: Two equal squares pushed together side by side make a rectangle: four straight sides, four corners, but longer than it is tall.
steps.narration: Two equal squares pushed together side by side make a rectangle: four straight sides, four corners, but longer than it is tall.

widget.prompt: Two equal squares are pushed together side by side. Tap the shape they make.

hotspots.label: square
hotspots.feedback: The result is longer than it is tall, so its sides are no longer all equal.

hotspots.label: triangle
hotspots.feedback: Joining two four-sided pieces cannot reduce the outline to three sides.

hotspots.label: circle
hotspots.feedback: Straight-edged squares keep straight edges however they are joined.

widget.missFeedback: Press the two squares together and trace the outside edge.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — two equal squares side by side make a rectangle.

predict.prompt: Two equal squares join side by side into a rectangle. How many sides does the rectangle have?
predict.reveal: The two joined edges hide inside. The two top edges line up into one long top side, and the two bottom edges make one long bottom — four sides in all: top, bottom, and the two ends.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g1s make rectangle.
invariants: A shape's defining attributes must stay fixed while colour, size and orientation vary.
misconceptions: Treating colour, size or orientation as if it decided what a shape is.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same shape?

explanationVariants: The rectangle's outline has four sides.

widget.prompt: Two equal squares are pushed together side by side to make a rectangle. How many corners does a rectangle have?

commonErrors.feedback: That counts the corners of both starting pieces; joining them hides the edges that meet inside.
That misses one corner of the finished rectangle; count all the way around the outside.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Look again at the shape's sides and corners, counting each one exactly once.

steps.body: The two equal squares are still visible as parts of the rectangle. Their shared side is an inside seam, not part of the finished outline.
steps.narration: The two equal squares are still visible as parts of the rectangle. Their shared side is an inside seam, not part of the finished outline.

widget.prompt: Two equal squares share one full side. Tap the part that becomes an inside seam of the rectangle.

hotspots.label: outside side
hotspots.feedback: An outside side stays on the rectangle's outline. The side the squares share becomes the inside seam.

hotspots.label: corner
hotspots.feedback: A corner is a point, not the full side where the two equal squares touch.

hotspots.label: gap
hotspots.feedback: The equal squares touch with no gap. Their shared full side becomes the inside seam.

widget.missFeedback: Look for the full side touched by both equal squares.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — the shared side becomes an inside seam, so it is not part of the outside outline.

widget.prompt: Two equal squares are placed side by side and joined. What shape results?

options.label: A rectangle
options.feedback: Correct — joining two equal squares side by side makes a rectangle because they share one full side.

options.label: A circle
options.feedback: Straight-sided pieces cannot join into a circle; every edge they contribute stays straight.

options.label: A cone
options.feedback: That is a solid, but joining flat pieces edge to edge keeps the result flat.

options.label: Nothing — shapes cannot be joined
options.feedback: Shapes combine readily; a new, larger shape is exactly what composing produces.

widget.prompt: A square is cut along one diagonal, leaving a triangle. How many corners does a triangle have?

commonErrors.feedback: That counts a corner twice, or counts the original square's fourth corner that this triangle does not use; trace only this triangle's own three corners.
That misses one corner of the finished triangle; count all the way around the outside.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Look again at the shape's sides and corners, counting each one exactly once.

widget.prompt: Which features make a rectangle a rectangle?

options.label: 4 straight sides and 4 square corners
options.feedback: Correct — a rectangle has 4 straight sides and 4 square corners; colour, size, and direction can change.

options.label: Painted a bright red colour
options.feedback: Color can change freely without the shape changing; it is not a defining attribute.

options.label: Made much bigger in size
options.feedback: Size can change freely without the shape changing; a tiny rectangle is still a rectangle.

options.label: Turned to face a new direction
options.feedback: Turning a shape does not change what it is; orientation is not a defining attribute.
